column1: # Named skins. An instance picks one by name in its site.yml, and a PUBLISH can
# override that for ONE build with the `theme` input on publish.yml, which
# reaches the engine as DOCRENDER_THEME (docrender/instance.py). The file is
# never written to, so an override cannot outlive the run that asked for it.
# STRUCK 2026-08-07: "a page or folder can override with `theme:` in
# frontmatter." NOTHING HAS EVER READ THAT KEY.
# Verified at HEAD before striking, three independent ways:
#   1. theme.build_css() takes NO ARGUMENTS. It reads state.INSTANCE and
#      nothing else -- there is no page, folder or path anywhere in its
#      signature, so there is no input a frontmatter key could arrive on.
#   2. assets._plan() calls it ONCE and links the result as a single
#      tokens.css from EVERY page in the build.
#   3. The CSS it emits is scoped to :root and to the two document-level
#      scheme attributes. Even a second sheet published for one subtree would
#      repaint the whole site.
# So a per-page theme is not merely unimplemented -- it is unbuildable in this
# shape. The line survived long enough to be read as a feature and asked about
# as one, which is the expensive kind of rot: A DOC THAT PROMISES AN EXTENSION
# POINT THAT DOES NOT EXIST costs more than a blank, because somebody plans
# against it. Struck rather than deleted, per the house rule on reversals --
# deleting it teaches nobody why it was wrong to believe.
# A genuinely scoped theme is SCOPED, NOT GREENLIT as next-build-spec.md
# BUILD 3 (specs/scoped-theme.md), and it is an architecture change to the
# theme spine rather than a variable read.
# `base` is always applied underneath whatever else is chosen, so a new theme
# only has to state what it CHANGES rather than redeclare every token.
theme
base
column3: shared token set, always applied under everything else
